better the devil you know phrase

also better the devil you know than the devil you don’t, a known evil is best

classical

Plaut. Trin. 63: nōta mala rēs optumast

Nōta mala rēs optima est.

a bad thing you know is the best kind

One old man’s answer to another who has proposed, in jest, that they exchange wives: keep yours as you got her; with one he did not know he would not know what to do.

Examples

  • nōta mala rēs optumast. Nam ego nunc sī ignōtam capiam, quid agam nesciam.

    a known evil is the best evil. For if I took on one I didn’t know now, I shouldn’t know what to do.Plaut. Trin. 63–64

See also evil.

SourcesLewis & Short: notus

Plautus, Trinummus 63–64.
